top_five.text: An escalating regional Ebola outbreak originating in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed more than 5,400 people among over 11,000 cases amid severe healthcare security disruptions.
Flash flooding across remote mountain valleys in Nepal and Tibet has killed at least 157 people and left hundreds more missing.
An armed gang attack in Kenscoff, Haiti, left at least 47 people dead, including five children, and resulted in the mass abduction of over 50 civilians.
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake in the southern Philippines killed at least 32 people, injured 200 others, and left 12 people missing.
Severe winter weather and ongoing bombardment in Gaza have worsened conditions for displaced families, with reports of children dying from cold exposure.

top_story.quote: An escalating Ebola outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed over 5,400 people and expanded regionally, severely compounded by armed attacks on healthcare facilities and high mortality among young children.
top_story.label: GLOBAL / CROSS-CUTTING — Escalating Regional Ebola Epidemic

Middle East.headline: OPT/Gaza — Military Strikes and Winter Flooding Deepen Humanitarian Crisis
Middle East.body: Severe winter weather and flooding in Gaza are worsening conditions for displaced Palestinians, with reports of children dying from cold exposure. International appeals, including from the European Union and over 50 countries, are demanding that Israel lift its blockade and reopen border crossings to permit immediate humanitarian aid and large-scale recovery. Concurrently, Israeli air strikes and artillery bombardment continue, including a drone strike near northern Gaza's Jabalia refugee camp that killed at least two Palestinians. Separately, the Israeli military reported striking a senior Hamas commander.

Middle East.headline: Yemen — Frontline Fighting and Siege Heighten Famine and Explosive Hazards
Middle East.body: A tightened siege by Houthi forces surrounding Yemen's third-largest city, Taiz, is raising fears of famine. Concurrently, renewed frontline hostilities in the area threaten communities already experiencing mass displacement, chronic food insecurity, and worsening child malnutrition. The HALO Trust warned that escalated fighting around Taiz poses a sharp risk of increased casualties from landmines and unexploded ordnance among civilians fleeing conflict zones.

Americas.headline: Haiti — Mass Gang Attack and Kidnapping in Kenscoff
Americas.body: The United Nations confirmed that armed men killed at least 47 people, including at least five children, and kidnapped over 50 others in Kenscoff, on the outskirts of Port-au-Prince. The incident is considered one of the largest mass kidnappings in Haiti in recent years. In a social media video, a gang leader threatened to kill all hostages if the Haitian National Police harm any gang members during rescue attempts.

Americas.headline: Haiti — Joint Anti-Gang Operations Near Port-au-Prince
Americas.body: Haitian authorities and El Salvador conducted joint operations against major criminal organizations near Port-au-Prince. Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele published footage of attack helicopters targeting a compound belonging to Wilson Joseph, leader of the 400 Mawozo gang. As many as 20 people were killed in the strike, though Joseph was reportedly absent. The operation follows a separate drone strike on November 6 that killed Mathias Saintil, head of the Boston gang in Cité Soleil.

Americas.headline: Venezuela — Earthquake Rescue Operations
Americas.body: Emergency efforts continue in Venezuela following earthquakes, with reports indicating that the window to locate survivors is closing. Venezuela sits near fault lines along the South American and Caribbean tectonic plates. The country faces critical challenges in building long-term resilience and emergency response infrastructure to protect lives during major seismic events.

Africa.headline: DRC — Uncontrolled Ebola Outbreak Exceeds 11,000 Cases Amid Attacks on Healthcare
Africa.body: An escalating Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths, making it the deadliest in the country's history. Containment efforts remain severely hindered by ongoing insecurity in eastern areas like Ituri. The World Health Organization verified 81 attacks on health facilities, which cut off response teams from more than 1,000 exposed individuals. The United Nations reported the epidemic is expanding rapidly across vast areas. The health emergency compounds a broader humanitarian crisis in DRC, where an estimated 28.8 million people face acute food insecurity.
verified_figures: More than 1,000 exposed people cut off from health responders

Africa.headline: Sudan — Inter-Tribal Violence Kills 50 and Drives Mass Displacement in Darfur
Africa.body: Severe armed clashes between the Rizeigat and Habbaniya tribes near the border of South and East Darfur have left more than 50 civilians dead and dozens wounded. The violence erupted near Al-Sunta and Al-Firdaws localities following long-standing disputes over livestock looting. The fighting triggered large-scale mass displacement as residents fled affected villages seeking safe havens.

Africa.headline: Kenya — Border Conflict Spillover Displaces Over 10,000 in Marsabit County
Africa.body: Spillover violence from armed conflict in Moyale, Ethiopia, has displaced more than 10,000 people across the border into Marsabit County, Kenya, according to local government officials. The displacement and continuous influx of refugees are placing severe pressure on local healthcare services in the host communities.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Russian strike targets cargo vessel and infrastructure at Chornomorsk port
Europe.body: Russian forces reportedly struck a cargo vessel and infrastructure in Ukraine's Black Sea port of Chornomorsk, according to Russian state media cited by Reuters. The strike targets key maritime transport infrastructure critical to regional logistics and trade. No immediate details were provided in the available reporting regarding casualties, the extent of damage, or the specific cargo aboard the targeted vessel.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — US-mediated peace talks stall over territorial proposals and energy truce rejection
Europe.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that recent US-mediated negotiations included proposals for Ukraine to cede the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, though discussions yielded no tangible progress. Zelensky also claimed Russia rejected a proposed energy truce. Meanwhile, French President Emmanuel Macron warned that limiting international aid to Ukraine would force Kyiv into an unjust peace and risk renewed war. European leaders have expressed concern over potential major US concessions to Moscow ahead of a planned summit involving US, Chinese, and Russian leadership.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Philippines — Magnitude 7.8 Earthquake Kills 32 and Injures 200 in South
Asia-Pacific.body: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck the southern Philippines, leaving at least 32 people dead, 200 injured, and 12 others missing, according to the Philippine civil defense agency. Search and rescue operations are ongoing amid reports that individuals may be trapped inside a damaged school. Tsunami warnings issued following the morning tremor have mostly been lifted while officials assess regional structural damage.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Myanmar — Military Airstrike Kills 12 at Rakhine Displacement Camp
Asia-Pacific.body: A Myanmar military airstrike targeted a displacement camp in Rakhine state, killing at least 12 people, including a five-year-old child, and wounding 18 others, according to local rescuers. The attack highlights severe protection risks facing internally displaced civilians in the state.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Indonesia — Magnitude 7.4 Offshore Earthquake Kills One and Damages Infrastructure
Asia-Pacific.body: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck off eastern Indonesia in the Molucca Sea between Sulawesi and Maluku, killing one person and damaging buildings. The early-morning tremor produced tsunami waves reaching up to 75 centimeters high and prompted regional tsunami warnings that were subsequently lifted. Structural damage and panic were reported in North Sulawesi province.
verified_figures: Tsunami waves up to 75 centimetres high

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Democratic Republic of the Congo — Regional Ebola Outbreak Escalates Past 5,400 Deaths
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Six months after being declared, an Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus continues to expand across the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with cases also reported in Kenya and Nigeria. Health agencies report over 11,000 cases and 5,437 deaths. Children account for more than a quarter of confirmed cases, and seven in ten infected children under five have died. Doctors Without Borders warned the outbreak remains out of control due to response dysfunctions and ineffective contact tracing. Meanwhile, Uganda has initiated a national Ebola preparedness workplan under IGAD, while the UAE partially eased travel restrictions on Ugandan nationals.
verified_figures: Children account for more than a quarter of confirmed cases and one third of deaths
7 in 10 children under five with confirmed Ebola have died

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Nepal / Tibet — Flash Floods Kill Over 150 People and Leave Hundreds Missing
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: A severe flash flood swept through remote valleys across Nepal and Tibet, destroying villages and causing extensive destruction. Nepali police confirmed that authorities have recovered 157 bodies, while dozens more are confirmed dead and hundreds remain missing. Emergency teams are working to relocate families from high-risk flood areas to safer locations, with the government promising full assistance for emergency rescue, shelter, food, and medical treatment.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: India — Successive Cyclones Threaten Coastal Andhra Pradesh
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Coastal areas in Andhra Pradesh, India, face additional storm risks as a new weather system brews over the Bay of Bengal. According to the India Meteorological Department, the system could intensify into a cyclonic storm. The development follows a month of severe weather caused by two successive cyclones, Arnab and Murasu, which battered the state.

escalation_risks.trigger: Continued tightening of the siege surrounding Taiz by Houthi forces alongside escalated frontline combat could completely sever vital supply lines.
escalation_risks.potential_impact: Accelerated risk of city-wide famine and increased civilian casualties from unexploded ordnance and landmines among fleeing populations.

escalation_risks.trigger: Retaliatory mobilization following clashes over livestock looting between the Rizeigat and Habbaniya tribes could ignite broader inter-communal warfare.
escalation_risks.potential_impact: Further civilian casualties, destruction of rural settlements, and mass displacement across South and East Darfur border areas.

escalation_risks.trigger: A developing low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal could intensify into a cyclonic storm making landfall within 72 hours.
escalation_risks.potential_impact: Renewed coastal flooding and infrastructure damage in areas recently affected by two successive tropical cyclones.
